transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you. Thank you so much for seeing me. Am I... is it okay if I sit here? 

Well, I'm here because... well, it's probably nothing too serious, I hope. I work as a cashier, and lately I've just been having these little... hiccups, I guess you could say, at the register. 

Sometimes I just sort of get stuck doing things that don't really fit the moment. Like, I might catch myself just tapping the scanner in a certain pattern, or... or I'll just freeze up entirely with my hand hovering right over the cash drawer while the customer is standing there waiting for their change. 

I don't mean to do it, I promise. I know it probably looks a little strange to people, and I feel terrible about making anyone wait. But my manager didn't really understand, and... well, I actually got written up for it last week, which is really embarrassing. I just want to be a good employee and do things right, you know? Does that... does that make sense?

When you catch yourself tapping the scanner or freezing, do you feel like you are doing it because you have a strong, uncomfortable urge to perform the action to prevent something bad from happening, or does it feel like your body is just doing it on its own without that kind of mental pressure?

Oh, um, thank you for breaking it down like that. That's a really good question. No, I wouldn't say it's an urge to prevent anything bad. I don't feel any pressure like that. 

Like I was mentioning before, it's more that... well, my body just sort of does it on its own, I guess. I just get stuck doing these things that really don't fit the moment. The tapping, or just freezing there with my hand over the drawer... it just happens, and then I realize the customer is waiting. I know it's probably just a silly habit I need to break, especially since it got me written up, and I really am trying my best to fix it so I can be a good cashier. 

Am I explaining that okay for you? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Besides these physical movements, do you ever find yourself making sudden, involuntary sounds or repeating words out loud when you don't intend to?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I don't make any sudden noises or... or repeat things out loud. I'm pretty quiet, actually. I try to be very polite and professional with the customers, so I definitely wouldn't want to be making any strange sounds or anything disruptive. 

It's really just those little physical pauses I mentioned. I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right answers. Is that... is that helpful?
Have you noticed any other physical changes, such as tremors in your hands, stiffness in your muscles, or times when you feel like your thinking is unusually slow or clouded?

Oh, um, no, I haven't noticed anything like that. My hands are steady, thankfully. No shaking or... or stiffness in my muscles. I feel pretty normal physically, aside from those little pauses I mentioned. 

And my thinking... well, I like to think I'm still pretty sharp. I really try my best to stay focused on the register and make sure I'm doing a good job for the store, so I haven't felt cloudy or slow or anything. I always want to make sure I'm paying attention to the customers. 

I hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of everything so I can get back on track at work. Did I answer that right for you?
Have you recently been diagnosed with any new medical conditions or started taking any new medications, even ones you might think are unrelated to these physical pauses?

Oh, um, no. No, nothing like that. I haven't been diagnosed with anything new, and I haven't started taking any new medications at all. 

I try to take really good care of myself, you know, so I can be reliable at work. I definitely wouldn't want to take anything that might mess up my performance at the register or cause any problems. So, it's just a clean bill of health on that front, thankfully. 

I hope that's helpful for you to know? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details so we can get this sorted out and I can get back in my manager's good graces. Am I doing okay with these questions?
How old were you when you first started noticing these physical pauses, and have they been happening consistently for more than a year?

Oh, well, I guess... um, I'm 54 now, and I suppose it's been going on for a little while. Not forever, though! Just, um, maybe about two years and four months, give or take? 

It seemed to start right around the time my youngest moved away to the Eastern Shore for college. You know how it is, the house gets a little quiet, and maybe I just started noticing things more. It hasn't been a huge problem the whole time, really, just sort of... building up a little bit lately, which is why my manager mentioned it. 

I hope it's okay that it's been going on for that long? I probably should have said something sooner, but I really didn't want to be a bother or make a big fuss over nothing. I try to handle things on my own, you know? Does that timeline make sense to you?
When you feel these pauses or tapping movements coming on, do you ever feel a physical sensation in your body, like a tingling or tension, that you can temporarily relieve by performing the action?

Oh, um, no... no, I don't think I feel anything like that. There's no tingling or... or tension building up, or anything that feels like an itch I have to scratch. It just sort of... happens, I guess? I don't do it to feel better or relieve any pressure in my body. 

I really hope that's not a bad thing to say? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the exact truth so I'm not wasting your time or leading you down the wrong path. I'm trying my absolute best to pay attention to how my body feels so I can give you good answers. Did I explain that okay for you?

During those moments when you freeze or tap the scanner, are you fully aware of everything happening around you, or does it feel like you are briefly 'zoning out' or losing track of your surroundings?

Oh, no, I'm definitely fully aware. I don't zone out at all, I promise. I can hear the customers, I can see the line, I know exactly what's going on around me. 

I'm actually a very attentive person, especially at work. I wouldn't want you to think I was just... daydreaming or ignoring people. It's just that my body sort of pauses, but my mind is right there, completely sharp. I'm always trying to make sure the customers are happy and the line keeps moving, even if I get a little stuck for a second. 

I hope that makes sense? I just really want to reassure you that my mind isn't wandering off on the job. I take my work very seriously. Is that the kind of answer you were looking for?
When you have these episodes, have you ever noticed your body or limbs taking on an unusual, awkward, or twisted position that you feel unable to correct for those few seconds?

Oh, um... well, no, my body doesn't really get twisted up or anything dramatic like that. I wouldn't want you to think I'm, you know, contorting myself at the register. It's nothing scary. 

It's more just... getting stuck in these little actions that don't really fit what I'm supposed to be doing right then. Like, um, I might just freeze with my hand hovering right over the open cash drawer, even though the customer is standing right there waiting for their change. Or I'll find myself tapping the barcode scanner on the counter in a little pattern instead of ringing up the next item. 

It's really just silly little things, but... well, I suppose it doesn't look great to the customers, and, um, my manager actually wrote me up for it last week. That's actually why I came in, to be honest. I really want to be a good employee and not cause any trouble for my boss. I hope it's not too terrible that I'm doing these things? I'm really trying my best to stop. Does that sound like what you were asking about?

When you are stuck in these moments, do you feel as though your muscles are 'locked' or 'stuck' in place against your will, or is it more like you simply lose the ability to initiate the next movement?

Oh, um... it's definitely not like my muscles are locked or anything like that. I wouldn't want you to think I'm having some kind of, you know, paralysis or anything scary. My muscles work just fine, I promise. 

It's more like... I just sort of... pause? Like I just don't start the next thing I'm supposed to do right away. It's just a little delay, really. I don't feel trapped in my own body or anything extreme. I just sort of lose the... the momentum for a second, I guess? 

I really hope that's an okay way to describe it. I don't want to make it sound worse than it is, because I really am trying hard to stay on track at work. Did I answer that the right way for you?
Do these pauses or tapping movements only happen while you are at work at the register, or do you find yourself doing them at home or in other situations as well?

Well, um... I guess I've noticed it a little bit at home, too. Not very often, I promise! Just, you know, maybe pausing while I'm making a cup of coffee or something. But it really only became an issue at work. 

I mean, I really didn't want to come in and bother you with it, but... well, like I mentioned before, the freezing with my hand over the cash drawer, or the tapping the scanner... it just doesn't fit what I'm supposed to be doing. And the customers are just standing there, waiting. I feel so bad about it. 

And, um, since my manager wrote me up last week... well, I just really want to fix it. I want to be a good employee and do my job right. I don't want to cause any more trouble for anyone. Is it okay that I'm mostly just worried about how it affects my job? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
When you catch yourself doing these things, do you feel that you have to perform them in a very specific, exact way, or that you have to repeat them until they feel 'just right'?

Oh, no, it's not like that at all. I wouldn't want you to think I have some sort of, um, obsession or compulsion where everything has to be perfect. I'm really not fussy like that, I promise! 

It's just... well, it just happens. I don't feel like I *have* to do it a certain way, or like I'm trying to get it "just right." It's more like I just sort of... drift off into doing it without really meaning to. And as soon as I realize I'm doing it, I just want to stop and get back to ringing up the customer. 

I really don't want to make a big deal out of it or sound like I have all these complicated rules in my head, because I really don't. I'm just trying to be a normal, helpful cashier. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your questions the way you need me to.
When you are walking, have you or has anyone else noticed that one of your arms doesn't swing as much as the other, or that you might be dragging a foot slightly?

Oh, um, no... I don't think so. I really haven't noticed anything like that, and nobody has ever said anything to me about how I walk. I mean, I walk just fine, I promise. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm stumbling around or dragging my feet at work or anything. I try to be very careful and, you know, walk normally. I'm pretty sure both my arms swing just like everyone else's. I really try hard to blend in and just do a good job. 

Is it okay that I haven't noticed anything like that? I hope I'm not missing something important you need to know. I'm really trying to give you the best answers I can.
When you are at home, do you ever find that it becomes difficult to complete a task that involves several steps, like following a recipe or organizing your belongings?

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I'm pretty organized at home, I think. I try to keep things tidy so I'm not a bother to anyone who comes over, not that I have a lot of company, but still. 

I can follow recipes just fine. I usually stick to simple things anyway, so there aren't too many steps to get confused by. I wouldn't want you to think I'm sitting at home unable to take care of myself or anything like that. I manage my own place, do my laundry... all the normal things. 

I might get a little distracted sometimes, maybe leave a cabinet door open or forget where I set down my keys for a second, but nothing major. Everyone does that sometimes, right? I just want to reassure you that I'm taking good care of my home life. I hope that's what you were asking?

When you catch yourself doing these things, do you ever have a specific, uncomfortable physical feeling—like an itch, a tickle, or a sense of 'not-rightness'—in the part of your body that is about to move?

Oh, um... no, I don't get any feelings like that. No itches or tickles or anything strange before it happens. I promise I don't have any weird sensations going on in my body. 

It really is just a... a little habit, I guess. Nothing uncomfortable or unusual leading up to it. I wouldn't want you to think I'm having these bizarre physical feelings, because I'm really not. It's just... it just happens, and then I stop it. 

I'm perfectly comfortable in my own skin, you know? I hope it's alright that I don't have those feelings you mentioned. I'm just trying to be as honest and helpful as I can be. Am I doing okay with these questions?
When you are at home, do you ever find yourself struggling to plan or sequence multiple tasks, such as preparing a meal that requires several steps?

Oh, um... no, not at all. I think we... we might have talked about this just a little bit ago, but I really don't have any trouble with that kind of thing. 

I make sure to plan things out so everything gets done properly. I usually just make simple meals anyway, like a sandwich or heating up some soup, so there's not much to get tangled up in. I wouldn't want you to worry that I can't feed myself or that I'm just sitting around confused. I do a good job keeping on top of my daily routine, I promise. 

I really try to be responsible and take care of myself. Is it helpful that I'm managing all of that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have you noticed any recent changes in your memory, such as forgetting the names of people you see often or losing track of the date or day of the week?

Oh, um... no, my memory is actually really good, I think. I haven't noticed any changes like that at all. 

Working at the register, you know, I see a lot of regular customers, and I always make a point to remember their names and say hello properly. I wouldn't want you to think my mind is slipping or that I'm getting confused about things like the date. I always know what day it is. I even keep a little calendar by my fridge just to be extra sure I'm on top of everything and not missing anything important. 

I really do try my best to stay sharp and present. I hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure I'm doing well with all these questions and giving you what you need.
Are you able to hold back or suppress these tapping movements or pauses if you make a conscious effort to do so while you are at work?

Oh, um... I really try to. I put in a lot of effort to just do my job the right way and be professional. But... well, I guess I should be completely honest with you, since that's sort of why I came in to see you in the first place. 

I want to be a good employee, I really do, but at the register, I keep getting... stuck, I guess. Doing these things that just don't fit the moment. Like, I'll catch myself tapping the barcode scanner in this specific pattern, or... or I'll just completely freeze, you know? With my hand hovering right over the cash drawer while the customer is just standing there waiting for their change. 

I try so hard to hold it back and just work normally, but... well, I'm a little ashamed to admit this, but last week it actually got me written up by my manager. I was so embarrassed. I really don't want you to think I'm a bad worker or that I don't care about my job, because I really do. I'm trying my absolute best to get it under control. 

Is it okay that I shared that with you? I know it doesn't sound great, but I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the right way and giving you what you need.
Have you noticed any changes in your personality or mood, such as feeling more irritable, sensitive, or impulsive, since these physical pauses began?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I really try to be a pleasant person to be around, you know? I haven't noticed feeling angry or snapping at anyone or anything like that. 

I always try to keep a smile on my face, especially at work with the customers, even when things get a little tricky with the pauses and everything. I wouldn't want you to think I'm becoming difficult or moody. I'm usually a very calm and steady person, and I think I've done a pretty good job of keeping my spirits up, all things considered. I really try to stay positive. 

I haven't been doing anything reckless or impulsive either. I like to think things through. Does that make sense? I hope it's a good thing that my mood hasn't really changed, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I'm doing.
When you were a child or teenager, did you ever experience any similar movements, like blinking, shoulder shrugging, or making strange sounds that you eventually grew out of?

Oh, um... no, I really don't think so. I was a pretty normal kid, I'd say. I never did anything like that, no strange noises or weird blinking or anything that would make people look at me funny. 

I always tried to be well-behaved and polite, even when I was little. I wouldn't want you to think I've always had these... these issues, or that there was something wrong with me growing up. I was just a regular teenager, you know? I did well in school and tried not to cause any trouble for my parents. 

I really can't remember anything like what you're describing. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you the history you need to figure this all out.
